seoTitle: Working During a UK PhD: Visa Conditions and University Rules
title: Working During a UK PhD: Visa Conditions and University Rules
content:
Your visa conditions, university rules and funding agreement can each limit outside work. Check all three before accepting a job, including how your institution defines term time for research students.

Check your own permission

Read the work conditions attached to your current immigration permission and confirm them with your university’s international student team. Many eligible full-time degree students have a term-time hours limit, but the permitted activity depends on the individual permission and sponsor. Use your actual conditions when considering an offer.

Confirm research-degree term time

Doctoral researchers do not necessarily follow the undergraduate holiday calendar. Ask the university to confirm your term and approved vacation dates in writing. Summer, writing-up time and office closures should not automatically be treated as permission to work full-time.

Check the activity as well as the hours

Certain activities, including self-employment, are restricted under Student permission. Do not assume freelance work, running a business or an unpaid role is permitted simply because the hours are low. Immigration guidance distinguishes volunteering from voluntary work, which can count towards the work limit. Ask about the precise activity before accepting it.

Review university and funding conditions

Your doctoral programme or award can impose additional restrictions or require approval. Read the funding agreement and discuss teaching or other duties with the relevant office. If you have several roles, consider the combined hours rather than each job separately.

Plan around confirmed arrangements

Keep employment records and the university’s guidance. Build a study budget from guaranteed funding rather than work you have not secured or confirmed as permitted. Completion and any later immigration application involve separate conditions; do not assume submitting a thesis automatically changes your right to work.

Official information

  • Official Student immigration rules
  • Official Student route guidance

Check the whole week, not each role separately

If you have more than one permitted role, consider the combined hours under your actual conditions. Confirm whether training, preparation or voluntary work counts in the circumstances, using university guidance and the relevant rules. Do not assume an unpaid position is unrestricted. Keep a written record of the advice and of your hours. For teaching or demonstrating, ask both the employer and graduate school how the role fits your appointment or studentship. Planning around confirmed permissions is safer than interpreting a general article as approval for a particular job.
